issues.body: `_park_call_site` still accepts any loop iterable whose live AST contains the bound name. For `targets if pending is not pending else []`, `_constant_truth` returns `None`, `_static_control` is false because the comparison contains `Name` nodes, and `_control_arms` marks both arms live; yet an ordinary local is identical to itself, so the condition is always false and the loop always receives `[]`. Likewise, `filter(lambda _: False, targets)` leaves the `targets` argument visible to `_live_nodes` and therefore certifies, although the filter can yield no element. These are the two concrete red tests requested in round three, and neither appears in the new refusal suite. Reachability of a name during evaluation does not prove that the resulting iterable contains the selected batch.
issues.fix_hint: Restrict accepted loop iterables to a structural grammar that guarantees iteration of the bound batch, preferably the bound name itself plus only explicitly justified transparent forms. Add a live control and named refusal tests for `targets if pending is not pending else []` and `filter(lambda _: False, targets)`, and verify that the production call site remains certified.
issues.title: Runtime-valued iterables still certify without iterating the bound batch

verdict.summary: The round-four change does not close the prior round's soundness finding. The checker still treats arbitrary runtime-bearing iterable expressions as acceptance evidence merely because the bound batch name is reachable during expression evaluation. Both bypasses named in round three remain accepted even though neither can iterate the selected batch, so parking can still be disabled while the production seam certifies. This is materially the same major finding at the same severity.
